title: ProbeFlow: Certified Search for Budgeted Information Design
subtitle: Corrected conference narrative edition · 26 October 2026 · certified search and a separate acquisition diagnostic

paper.heading: Abstract
paragraphs: Information design and sequential prediction have different objectives and different opportunities for improvement. ProbeFlow develops a certified single-winner search for the fixed-subset problem of minimizing the worst sharp conditional loss-interval width under a hard query budget. Verified feasible readings supply lower bounds for the outer subset minimization, while partial-transcript widths supply upper bounds for the inner maximization. Exact lexicographic selection and an absolute epsilon certificate replace the earlier all-tie output contract.

Seven constructed conditions, four solvers and three cold cyclic orders yield 84 completed runs. In the hardest eight-coordinate condition, all exact solvers return risk 21/64 and the same unique design; observed median CPU is 0.71875 s for a strong memoized value-only DP and 0.28125 s for exact branch-and-bound, with maximum traced Python peaks 334,535 and 141,338 bytes. Joint CPU/peak wins occur in only 2/7 conditions. A separate participant-balanced acquisition estimator on 524 previously exposed windows is coherent but regresses, ties its fixed/myopic controls and has no independent final participants. We therefore claim bounded engineering gains and conditional certificates, with no accuracy improvement, universal speedup or population-safety claim.

paper.heading: 1. Introduction
paragraphs: Choosing a fixed set of measurements under a hard budget requires solving two nested problems: select the query set, then account for its worst feasible reading. When uncertainty is represented by sharp intervals for a loss contrast, a useful design minimizes the largest remaining interval width. Exhaustively returning every tied design and every worst reading can make this computation expensive even when a user needs only one reproducible optimum.

ProbeFlow addresses that computational gap in the retained public-world model. It returns one canonical risk/cost/mask winner, or a feasible design with an absolute epsilon certificate. Verified complete readings lower-bound the outer subset minimization; partial transcripts upper-bound the inner maximization. Separating these directions permits safe pruning. A value-only subset dynamic program supplies a strong comparison with the same inner kernel, cache rights, warm start and global floor.

The contributions are the single-winner/epsilon contract, code-matched exactness and certificate arguments, and a matched seven-condition engineering comparison that retains all negative cases. Exact branch-and-bound lowers both CPU and traced peak in only two of seven conditions; it leaves the exact objective unchanged. Branch-and-bound and dynamic programming themselves are established tools, and the present evidence does not establish external novelty or superiority over a reproduced published implementation.

A separate application diagnostic asks whether one participant-balanced row law improves sequential prediction and purchase decisions. Its objective J differs from fixed-subset interval width R. The coherent estimator regresses on exposed DEV and ties its fixed/myopic controls. Keeping that negative diagnosis separate tests the boundary between internal consistency, computation and application utility. Sections 3–4 define the two problems and methods, Section 5 reports their distinct experiments, and Sections 6–7 interpret the observations and limits.

paper.heading: 2. Related work and comparable rights
paragraphs: Active feature acquisition chooses observations and terminal predictions [1, 2]. The closest selected primary source already contains fixed predictors, terminal risks, conditional acquisition kernels, hard budgets and Bellman comparison [8]. Our participant-balanced row construction is not a new Bellman principle or joint predictor training. Learning-To-Measure pretrains then freezes a predictor and learns conditional/meta-policy structure [9]; SEFA uses latent gradient/Monte Carlo acquisition and grants a test availability mask in its selected availability experiment [10]. AFAPE concerns counterfactual acquisition-plus-misclassification cost under identification and positivity assumptions [11]. Local count support is not whole-policy identification.

The fixed-subset worst-width objective instead commits to queries before reading their closed bins. The retained complementarity witness violates diminishing returns, so a greedy warm start has no transferred adaptive-submodularity guarantee [7]. Branch-and-bound, lower bounds and exact subset DP are established general ideas; this study evaluates the specified variant and certificates, not external novelty, AO* correspondence or an external implementation benchmark. Repeated exposed-DEV selection remains a separate concern [3].

Table 1 summarizes selected-source rights rather than published numerical performance. Its audit read selected HTML sections and official metadata, with inherited capture/prefix limits retained separately. Full-paper proofs and code were not reproduced. A representation invariant to item order does not make deadlines, failures or stateful cache behavior order invariant.

paper.heading: 3. Problem formulation
paragraphs: Fixed-subset design. A nonempty compatible-world set Omega defines an original route-minus-static macro loss contrast Delta. Query i has positive integer price c_i and a guaranteed closed-bin observation relation. Choose subset S before any readings. A feasible transcript z restricts the original worlds to Omega(S,z), with sharp endpoints L(S,z) and U(S,z). Empty intersections are impossible readings, never zero endpoints. Closed bins overlap at their threshold, so a boundary world can support both labels.

The exact representative minimizes the tuple (R(S),c(S),mask(S)) subject to c(S)<=Q. Risk is the maximum conditional interval width over feasible complete readings. The original all-tie contract additionally returned every affordable primary-risk mask and every worst transcript. The new contract returns one canonical representative and one worst witness per completed risk. An epsilon guarantee concerns absolute macro-loss interval-width units, not accuracy percentages or relative prediction regret.

Sequential prediction. A public state contains paid values/tokens, successful groups S_a, all attempted groups T_a, remaining cap and permitted cache/history metadata. STOP uses the current frozen predictor; ABSTAIN incurs a specified loss. Every attempt is charged, including failures in contracts that contain failure. Current cached DEV has successful returns only, so its attempt and success sets coincide; physical provider reliability is unmeasured. Gold labels and full feature caches are evaluator-only inputs.

equations.explanation: Minimize this width under the query budget, then price and integer mask. It is not the application objective J.
Participant means precede equal-person averaging. E counts errors on predictions, A abstentions and C attempted quotes; every planned n_s must be positive.

The completed cached-DEV study includes abstention but no observed failure outcomes. The general failure branch is an explicit future/application contract, not measured sensor behavior.

paper.heading: 3.1. Sharp loss intervals
paragraphs: The search objective is defined by a finite-participant uncertainty set, not an empirical classification score. Participant j has n_j coordinates, requested coordinates A_j and known stop errors E_j. Requested binary errors share one global cap B_err across all participants; known stop errors equal one and other stop errors equal zero. Independent route/static availability vectors r and v lie in the unit box and each have participant sum n_j/2. The fixed cost is c=1/20 and k is nonnegative.

Let a_ji indicate a requested coordinate. Its route success is a_ji r_ji. The following losses charge a base route quote plus a requested quote, or two static quotes; k charges failed acquisition. Their equal-person difference Delta is optimized over the declared errors and availability constraints. A query observes a static-availability bin with threshold t_i in (0,1). No new participant, prediction or sensor reading is generated in the constructed search comparison.

The common endpoint routines optimize these original losses exactly over feasible error placements and box/sum vertices. The global binary cap is not duplicated for each participant. Query observations restrict the same original world set; they do not replace its unknown errors with labels or favorable zeros. This retained world model is what allows the different solvers and the raw-only independent checks to agree on an identical R.

equations.explanation: Per-coordinate route loss; a is the fixed requested-coordinate indicator.
Per-coordinate static loss, with its independently constrained availability vector.
Sharp L and U are respectively the minimum and maximum Delta over the nonempty compatible original worlds.

paper.heading: 4. Method
paragraphs: The primary method solves the fixed-subset R problem with a certified outer frontier and an exact inner width calculation. The separate acquisition diagnostic uses the same explicit information ledger to construct a conditional surrogate and execute paid decisions; it does not optimize R or train a new predictor.

paper.heading: 4.1. Certified subset search
paragraphs: An outer node (I,U) represents all affordable subsets between included I and M=I union U. For any verified feasible complete reading on M, projecting its labels to a represented S gives Omega(M,z_M) contained in Omega(S,z_S). Hence the width of that one M reading lower-bounds R(S). Maximizing over a fixed finite bank of such feasible readings remains a valid lower bound. M may itself be too expensive: it is an optimistic relaxation, not a design that the returned policy executes.

The implementation fixes three public-model worlds: all availability coordinates 1/2, a participant vertex that fills its required n_j/2 mass from the first coordinate, and its reversal. It validates box/mean/error-cap constraints and closed-bin membership. Projected duplicate readings are evaluated once. The resulting bound is cached by M. Positive query prices let the search remove individually unaffordable undecided items and use (LB,c(I),mask(I)) as a lexicographic lower tuple.

Inside a fixed subset, a partial transcript h contains the worlds of any completed descendant z. Its sharp width therefore upper-bounds descendant width. A completed feasible reading supplies the inner lower incumbent b. Cutting prefix width<=b preserves the numeric maximum and one existing witness, while the original all-tie traversal requires a strict inequality. A partial completed maximum can abandon an outer loser only when its full risk/cost/mask tuple cannot beat the exact incumbent.

Algorithm 1 combines these different bound directions. Greedy supplies only an exactly evaluated feasible warm start, without a submodularity claim. The frontier covers unresolved subsets and every incumbent comes from an exact feasible risk. At epsilon = 0 the search resolves remaining cheaper equal-risk subsets rather than stopping at scalar gap zero. At positive epsilon, the incumbent upper risk minus the minimum frontier lower bound certifies scalar regret. A handled resource interruption returns uncertified state and restores the active node if present; it does not resume or retry.

Inner maximization: partial-prefix width is an upper bound. The preseal direction witness has R(empty)=1/2 and R({1})=1/3; using the former as an outer lower bound would be invalid.

paper.heading: 4.2. Guarantees and the strong DP control
paragraphs: Proposition 1 (canonical exactness). Assume exact sharp endpoints, positive prices and verified feasible seed readings. If the zero-tolerance search terminates without interruption, its returned tuple is the minimum affordable (R,cost,mask). Each retained outer node covers its affordable descendants; removing an individually unaffordable item removes no such descendant. The node lower tuple is no larger than any represented tuple. Thus every pruned node is unable to improve the exact incumbent, while branching covers all remaining subsets. Empty-frontier termination proves the claim. Inner equality pruning preserves the numeric R and one witness, which is the output contract needed by this proof.

Proposition 2 (absolute certificate). At a positive-tolerance stop, every unresolved design is represented by a frontier lower bound and every resolved loser cannot improve the incumbent. Hence L_F is a lower bound on the global optimum and UB is a feasible upper bound. Subtracting these inequalities gives returned-risk regret at most UB-L_F, which is at most epsilon. This scalar statement does not certify the cheapest mask among equal-risk subsets. Handled timeouts are explicitly uncertified.

The strong comparison is a memoized value-only subset DP, rather than a traversal that repeats acquisition permutations. Its state M determines remaining budget Q-c(M), and its recurrence compares stopping with every affordable extension. Positive additions cannot lower price or integer mask. If R(M) reaches the shared global seed floor, M is already the canonical winner of its extension family and the DP may stop there. The same exact inner kernel, cold endpoint/local/risk caches, warm-start construction and global floor are granted to both methods.

Bound and cache overhead can exceed the saved search work. General affordable subsets and subset/reading pairs still grow exponentially, up to 2^N and 3^N before feasibility reductions. Fraction bit lengths, endpoint work, frontier storage and retained output also matter. Greedy is only a feasible warm start: a retained complementarity fixture has R(4)=R(5)=R(6)=3/8 and R(7)=1/4, so a diminishing-returns shortcut would lack its required premise.

equations.explanation: The exact tuple is tau(M)=(R(M),c(M),mask(M)). A_Q(M) contains the affordable items outside M.
All minima use the same lexicographic order; an empty extension family gives an infinite tuple. Terminal or floor-reaching states retain tau(M).

paper.heading: 4.3. Separate coherent-estimation diagnostic
paragraphs: The application study holds an inherited forest/prediction bank fixed and compares three estimators. Legacy empirical uses T-window-uniform risks/transitions. Legacy statewise shrinks calibration errors toward T risk while retaining T transitions. The coherent estimator first forms participant-balanced complete-row laws P_T and P_C, then mixes (64 P_T+192 P_C)/256 before conditioning. The state-dependent T/C proportions are generally not 1/4 and 3/4. One row law supplies terminal risks, next-token probabilities and initial-token mass.

Algorithms 2 and 3 match the frozen code. Common support requires at least 30 T rows and fitting participants 5 and 6 at the current state and every positive T-or-joint successor. Unsupported current states force STOP. Supported fixed orders with a blocked next action retain the better STOP/ABSTAIN decision, without replacing the query. Total budgets 1,2,3 include paid group 0; quote loss is 1/20 and abstention 2/5. Mask 15 and budget 4 are outside the seven-mask bank. All ten global orders may stop/abstain after revealed histories, making them stronger than fully committed subsets.

Under a sufficient finite state, nonnegative prices, a decreasing attempt horizon and common terminal rights, backward induction minimizes the declared surrogate. Legacy statewise risks and T transitions still define a valid abstract terminal-cost MDP; they need not represent the same complete-row predictive law. For the coherent law, partitioning compatible rows proves direct conditional tree loss equals recursive value. Myopic one-step value differs from eventual replanning-tree loss and is checked separately. These are algebraic identities, not population calibration. The estimator change bundles participant weighting, risks, kernels and initial mass, rather than identifying the causal effect of coherence alone.

paper.heading: 4.4. Frozen planning and paid execution
paragraphs: Policy tables and the selected fixed reference are frozen using T/C before the DEV bank is opened. Runtime selection sees purchased tokens and its frozen table, not current unpurchased values or labels. In this all-success replay, a selected reveal increments attempted/successful masks and consumes one quote. The purchased cache has no additional acquisition right. The evaluator records full denominator, abstention and paired-error partitions after decisions.

paper.heading: 5. Experiments
paragraphs: We evaluate computational efficiency for R and descriptive application loss for J in separate studies. Shared framing makes the comparison rights and denominators explicit; it does not pool their outcomes or treat repeated solver/policy paths as new application samples.

paper.heading: 5.1. Setup, comparators and measurement
paragraphs: The search study freezes seven constructed conditions: equality ties, impossible bins, zero shared-error cap with unequal prices, complementarity, a shared-cap tie case, and four independent two-coordinate pairs at budgets 2 and 4. There are four solvers and three cold cyclic orders, giving 84 planned and completed runs. Cyclic orders are descriptive repeated measurements, not independent application samples or a complete four-position Latin balance. The original all-tie solver is unchanged; value-only DP and both B&B variants share the exact one-witness inner routine, cold caches, greedy candidates and global seed floor.

Arm CPU/wall and tracemalloc peaks include validation, applicable seed construction, warm starts, endpoint/bound/cache/search work and raw event writes. Common imports, terminal receipt serialization and independent oracle have separate recorded scopes. The original all-tie endpoint-call counter excludes impossible-bin attempts, whereas its raw event stream retains those None readings. We disclose that definition rather than comparing unequal counts as the same primitive. Python allocation peak is not RSS, physical I/O or acquisition energy.

The application comparison reuses 514 complete fitting rows: T participants 5/6 have 168/154 rows and C 96/96. Three estimators, twelve policies and three total budgets produce 108 tables and 56,592 paths on the same 524 previously exposed DEV windows from participants 7/8 (266/258). No predictor is fitted or run anew. All current paths complete; failed/unknown/unstarted are 0 under cached successful returns. Independent final participants remain 0. Direct raw-only audits and distinct normal native review tasks inspect both studies without rerunning their producer experiments.

paper.heading: 5.2. Primary search results
paragraphs: All exact solvers agree on risk and the canonical design in every condition. The hard Q4 case has a unique mask 85 and risk 21/64; Q2 has mask 5 and risk 51/128. In Q4, median CPU is 6.96875 s for original all-tie,0.71875 s for strong DP and 0.28125 s for exact B&B. Maximum Python peaks are 231,943/334,535/141,338 bytes. The DP and exact B&B endpoint-call counts are 1,476 and 330 under their common counter; original all-tie reports 1,411 actual feasible calls under its distinct definition.

Exact B&B beats DP in both median CPU and maximum traced peak on complementarity and hard Q4, 2/7 conditions. Equality, impossible bins, zero-cap, shared-cap ties and hard Q2 preserve DP wins or ties. The shared-cap DP result is 0.203125 s versus 0.25 s for exact B&B and 85,789 versus 137,717 bytes. Table 2 retains all seven conditions; the supplement includes all four solvers and recorded work counters.

At epsilon = 1/32 every observed finite-oracle regret is 0, while hard Q4 has lower 97/320, upper 21/64 and certificate gap 1/40. Epsilon uses 14 outer nodes versus 47 for exact search. Exact objective gain is 0/no_gain. Figure 4 reports the hard-Q4 computational measurements.

Epsilon has a saved 1/40 certificate gap, not an exactness claim.

paper.heading: 5.3. Separate acquisition results
paragraphs: The coherent adaptive policy ties its selected fixed order and myopic control on every observed path at all budgets. At budgets 2 and 3 its macro J is 157023/457520, approximately 0.34320. At budget 3 the empirical adaptive J is 1364/4515 and statewise J is 10141/39216; coherent therefore regresses by 8059/196080 and 58067/686280 respectively. Figure 5 shows the full budget contrast, including budget 1 ties.

At coherent budget 3, participants 7/8 have errors 52/29, abstentions 100/45 and quotes 392/437. The 81 errors are accompanied by 145 abstentions. Against empirical, both policies predict on 379 windows with 5 corrections and 12 harms; 145 switch to abstention. Against statewise, the both-predict subset has 296 windows with 1 correction and 0 harms, plus 145 switches to and 83 from abstention.

The historical follow-up failed on unavailable mask 15 metadata and an exact-arithmetic abstention bug, with 0/12,576 DEV paths started. The failed run remains separate from the completed present study. All current 56,592 paths complete under cached successful returns; independent final participants remain 0.

Curves are participant-macro full loss including abstention and attempted quotes. Right: budget 3 paired-error and abstention partitions; corrections/harms use only both-predict windows. No confidence intervals or physical-cost inference.

paper.heading: 6. Discussion
paragraphs: The search result supports an engineering claim under an unchanged objective. Equality pruning removes work because one numeric maximum and one witness suffice; the outer feasible-reading bound can then eliminate subsets before exact evaluation. The matched DP already merges repeated subset orders and has the same warm-start and cache rights, so the Q4 contrast cannot be attributed solely to comparison with an all-tie enumerator. Which saved operations account for the timing difference was not isolated causally. Bound computation and frontier/cache overhead can offset pruning, consistent with the five conditions without a joint CPU/peak win.

A certificate and an observed optimum answer different questions. The hard-Q4 incumbent happens to match the finite oracle, but its saved lower bound leaves gap 1/40. Reporting that gap preserves what the search knew at termination. Similarly, exact objective gain 0 is expected when both methods solve the same problem. Lower computation cost may make that solution easier to obtain; it does not supply an accuracy gain or a larger information-design benefit.

The application diagnosis shows why coherent estimation is a method property rather than an improvement theorem. A common row law makes recursive values agree with direct conditional tree loss. It does not make that law calibrated on a new population. The revision jointly changes participant weighting, risks, transitions and initial mass, so the observed regression does not identify coherence as its cause. The pathwise fixed/myopic/adaptive tie provides no observed advantage from extra planning in this policy family. Counting only 81 errors would also omit 145 abstentions and their cost in J; both-predict corrections and harms must be read with the abstention partitions.

Together the studies locate the supported contribution: conditional certificates and bounded computational improvements for R, alongside a negative exploratory diagnostic for J. The earlier local positive and failed follow-up have different support and terminal contracts and cannot establish unchanged-system progress. A matched external implementation and a newly frozen, untouched final evaluation are follow-up requirements. They are not measured results in this edition.

paper.heading: 7. Limitations
paragraphs: The search proofs require the stated static immediate closed-bin world model, verified feasible seed readings, positive prices and correct sharp endpoints. General subsets/readings remain exponential (up to 2^N/3^N), with rational bit, cache, frontier and retained-output costs in addition. Seven small constructed conditions do not establish asymptotic or universal speedup. Greedy is a feasible incumbent heuristic, not a certificate; the original full-tie and new one-winner contracts cannot be conflated.

Resource guards are cooperative. Independent review found that the generic node guard tests counter>cap and a final callback/pop may increment after the last check, allowing a possible one-node overshoot on that final step. All 84 observed arms are far below 250,000, with no observed cap violation or invalid certificate. We preserve the frozen code and disclose this general boundary; a strict ceiling requires a separate corrected implementation and boundary regression. Timeouts remain explicitly uncertified. No OS isolation is claimed.

The application has no untouched final participant, provider-failure process, physical sensor cost, clinical validation or external-method reproduction. Coherent conditionals do not guarantee transport; support counts do not certify density, positivity or safety. No-eviction persistent DAG caching has the same ancestor-union cost for a fixed acquired set under any order; only different sets/STOP or additional cache assumptions can change that comparison. Static controls receive the same cache rights. Historical fit, authoring cost, RSS and complete deployment cost remain unmeasured.

paper.heading: 8. Conclusion
paragraphs: ProbeFlow provides certified single-winner and epsilon search for the stated information-design problem. CPU/peak improvements over strong DP occur in two of seven conditions. The separate coherent acquisition estimator instead yields ties and regressions.

supplement.heading: A.1. Original loss model and sharp endpoints
paragraphs: For participant j, binary requested errors have one shared global count cap B, known stop-error coordinates are fixed 1 and other stops 0. Independent route/static availability vectors lie in[0,1]^n and each sum to n/2. Requested route success uses r_i; nonrequested route success is 0. Route loss is (1-success_i)u_i+c(1+requested_i)+k requested_i(1-r_i). Static loss is (1-v_i)u_i+2 c+k(1-v_i), with c=1/20,k>=0. Delta is their equal-participant macro difference.

Sharp endpoints optimize this original loss over feasible binary-error placements and availability box/sum sets, preserving one global cap instead of duplicating it for each person. Query thresholds use closed intervals[0,t_i] and[t_i,1]; boundary worlds can support both labels. An impossible conjunction is distinct from an empty statistical denominator and cannot be filled with a favorable zero. Historical full derivations, shared-cap dynamic programming/heap and failed shortcuts are retained below.

supplement.heading: A.2. Outer lower bound proof
paragraphs: At node(I,U), let M=I union U and let S be any represented affordable design. A verified feasible reading z_M induces z_S by projection. Since Omega(M,z_M) is contained in Omega(S,z_S), sharp lower endpoints can only decrease and upper endpoints can only increase when passing to S. Thus W(M,z_M)<=W(S,z_S)<=R(S). Taking the maximum over a finite bank of feasible M readings preserves a lower bound for every S. M need not be affordable: additional information is an optimistic relaxation, never an executed purchase.

The bank contains exactly three predetermined public-model worlds: midpoint availability, a participant box/sum vertex formed by filling n/2 from the first coordinate, and its reverse. Set route availability to 1/2 and requested errors to 0; known stop errors remain fixed. Validate every box, mean, cap and closed-bin membership. Projected duplicate label vectors are evaluated once. The bound cache key is M because this bank and its projected-reading width depend on M rather than the particular I/U partition.

All prices are positive. Any individually unaffordable undecided item can be removed; adding items cannot lower c(I) or the integer bitmask. Therefore(LB,c(I),mask(I)) is a lexicographic lower tuple for every represented design. Pruning this tuple when it is no better than an exact incumbent preserves the canonical risk/price/mask representative.

supplement.heading: A.3. Inner upper bounds, lost ties and a wrong-direction example
paragraphs: For fixed S, a prefix h defines a superset of each descendant complete world set. Consequently L(h)<=L(z)<=U(z)<=U(h). A completed feasible width b lower-bounds the inner maximum; W(h)<=b may prune while retaining numeric maximum and an already stored witness. It may remove further maximizing readings. Original full-tie traversal must instead use W(h)<b. The new output deliberately gives one witness and does not retroactively satisfy the all-tie contract.

A completed partial maximum is also a lower bound on R(S), so a risk evaluation can stop early only when its full tuple cannot improve the outer incumbent; such a partial value is not cached as an exact risk or used to update the incumbent. The preseal direction fixture has n=[2],a=[1],e=[1],B=0,k=0 and thresholds 1/3: R(empty)=1/2 while R(first query)=1/3. Parent width is therefore not a valid outer lower bound. Complementarity separately gives R(4)=R(5)=R(6)=3/8 and R(7)=1/4, rejecting a stale greedy marginal upper bound.

supplement.heading: A.4. Frontier certificate and canonical exact stopping
paragraphs: Frontier nodes cover unresolved feasible subsets. Exact-pruned nodes cannot beat the incumbent, and every incumbent has an exact feasible risk. Set UB=R(incumbent), L=min(UB,min_frontier LB), or L=UB when the frontier is empty. Then L<=R*<=UB. At epsilon>0, UB-L<=epsilon certifies absolute returned-risk regret. At epsilon = 0, a scalar zero gap alone does not settle cheaper equal-risk masks, so the implementation resolves the lexicographic frontier.

A handled interruption restores an active popped node if it exists and returns uncertified saved state. It does not resume, rerun or assert success from coincident scalar bounds. A preseal zero-CPU case checks uncertified exhaustion; no registered main arm exhausted. Generic strict node-cap enforcement has a disclosed last-step possible+1 overshoot; all observed counts are far below the registered cap. The frozen implementation remains unchanged.

supplement.heading: S2. Original module and acquisition contract
paragraphs: The original state records disclosed values/mask separately from acquired sources and computed analyses. An action has source prerequisites, computation prerequisites, a public output contract, an incremental quote and an availability/failure outcome. The controller receives only outputs authorized by purchased public history. A raw source cached inside the executor cannot be inferred to be publicly disclosed, and a revealed statistic cannot authorize all related statistics. The sufficiency claim depends on history-consistent resource transitions and future-observation distributions.

This distinction matters in both comparisons and implementation. Charging each of three statistics for the same already-acquired trace would alter policy rankings through a ledger error. Granting a controller an internally computed prerequisite would instead alter its information set. The historical cache/disclosure construction is an authored design; the grouped-source experiments do not separately isolate every proposed state component or prove a general POMDP reduction.

A correct history audit therefore checks the same frozen predictor, identical public observations and marginal ledger, STOP rights, and failed-attempt accounting. When every action discloses a whole source group and cache state can be reconstructed from the mask, a richer cache state may add no independent predictive information. Complementary features can still defeat one-step value heuristics. These two modeling observations should not be confused with an observed advantage for the full proposed architecture.

supplement.heading: S5. Partial identification: assumptions that changed the answer
paragraphs: At zero failure penalty W2 gives a conditional route-static contrast 9653/2776800 when all requests succeed. Its eighteen-cell calculation varies a common failure rate q and an additional penalty k, with the conditional independence break-even 9653/114400 at k=0. The interval includes unknown G3 fallbacks on 129 requested windows. A sensitivity grid is an algebraic model over existing traces; no failed or delayed target attempt was observed.

W5 optimizes dependence between failure and loss rather than inserting independence. For participant-specific marginal failure q=1/20,k=0, its Delta bounds are [-59767/2776800,9653/2776800], whereas the independence value is 1311/925600. Both strict rankings remain possible. The route-universal threshold under that family is q>1283653/1388400, a conditional sharp statement that differs from the independence break-even. The pooled-opportunity family weights a different set of opportunities and is separately tabulated.

W6 distinguishes pointwise-uniform availability from a participant mean and shared G3 fallback from separate acquired-window fallbacks. With both success marginals 1/2 and k=0, pointwise-uniform/shared fallback yields the point value -15849/925600; separate fallback admits [-388477/2776800,293383/2776800]. Merely reporting the same average availability hides the relevant placement and coupling assumptions. Its one/two-window constructions are counterexamples, not new measurements.

W7 shows that learning an upper or exact count of fallback errors need not resolve policy sign. At half success and k=0, fixing every unknown requested error to zero shrinks width by about 92.26 percent yet leaves both strict rankings possible. At k=1/20 the saved example is route-strict up to error cap four, but cap five crosses zero. W8 adds guaranteed availability bins at known stop-error windows; low and high readings can favor opposite policies. An error count, a queried availability value and a failure observation are different data. [C09-C11]

supplement.heading: S6. Shared-cap endpoint reconstruction and sharpness
paragraphs: For fixed subset S and bin reading z, let Omega(S,z) contain the binary requested errors and rational availability vectors satisfying all declared constraints. The sharp endpoints are min and max of Delta over this set, not a confidence interval for a sampled population parameter. A feasible world for the lower endpoint may differ from the upper-endpoint world. Empty Omega is an impossible reading and remains distinct from execution failure.

For a fixed local binary error placement, each availability optimization is linear over l_i<=x_i<=h_i with sum x_i=m. Feasibility is sum l_i<=m<=sum h_i. Start at l; sort coefficients ascending for minimization or descending for maximization; allocate the remaining mass up to each h_i-l_i. A pairwise transfer from a worse to a better coefficient improves any allocation violating this order. This proves exactness for fixed binary errors. Enumerate the binary placements for each exact count j and retain both extrema.

Across participants use weights 1/(P*n_j). The min/max convolution combines local exact-count curves under a single total count <=B. Replicating B at every participant admits worlds outside the original model; pooling weights instead changes the estimand. W14 measured both errors in constructed controls. W12 also exposed competition for availability mass when prior slack is insufficient, so a simplified independent sorting expression from the restricted parent regime must not be used as a general sharp oracle.

W15 performs this endpoint calculation for every feasible bin transcript of every fixed subset and takes its maximum width. The exact all-subset selector and the original-world reference have equal public information, budget and objective. Their equality establishes implementation consistency; any improvement over that exact reference would signal either a changed problem or an error.

supplement.heading: S7. Prefix bounds, output completeness and rejected shortcuts
paragraphs: A partial reading creates a larger world set than any completion. Its sharp interval contains every completed interval, even though a difference between the two endpoints is not itself an endpoint realized by one world. Width containment is enough for an upper bound on the inner maximum. The incumbent b comes only from a completed feasible transcript; a prefix before any such leaf cannot justify pruning by an invented incumbent.

Strict comparison is required by the requested output, not just by conservative numerics. If an internal upper width equals b, some descendants can be additional worst-transcript ties. The saved zero-width example and W22 equality example show such losses under an equality cutoff. Bounds that are safe for finding one numeric maximum may be insufficient for listing all maximizers. Subset primary ties and worst-transcript ties are distinct collections and both are preserved.

The non-submodular construction has nested masks 4 subset 5 and adds the same remaining item: risk stays 3/8 from mask4 to6, but drops from 3/8 at5 to1/4 at7. For F(S)=R(empty)-R(S), the latter marginal is 1/8 while the former is zero. This falsifies diminishing returns for this declared objective, so stale-marginal lazy greedy has no transferred certificate. It neither refutes the published Bayesian adaptive-submodularity theorem nor proves every alternate prior/model non-submodular.

W19 maintains DFS coverage records for feasible leaves, impossible subtrees and strictly pruned subtrees; the disjoint completion counts reconcile to the full subset label family. A safe upper for R(S) cannot eliminate S in the outer minimization as though it were a lower bound. W22 preserves a numeric example with upper1/2, outer incumbent1/3 and exact mask2 value1/3: confusing bound direction would lose an affordable primary tie. [C15-C18]

supplement.heading: S8. Local envelopes and shared marginal allocation proof
paragraphs: Expand the unweighted local original loss difference as D=C-k*sum_A r+sum_E v+T, where C=-(n-a)(c+k)+k*m, m=n/2 and T=sum_A u_i(v_i-r_i). Write l_A,h_A,l_E,h_E,l_O,h_O for aggregate box bounds. Then rL=max(0,m-(n-a)), rU=min(a,m), eL=max(l_E,m-h_A-h_O), and eU=min(h_E,m-l_A-l_O). Summing w(C-k*rU+eL) and w(C-k*rL+eU) yields the common base [L0,U0].

For an exact requested-error count b, the coupling term is bounded below by -min(b,a-l_A) and above by min(b,h_A). Optimizing each sign correction over global sum b_j<=B gives f_j(b)=w_j min(b,c_j). Solving these corrections independently from the base relaxes coupling inside a participant, so the resulting interval is outward and need not be sharp. Solving the shared global cap is tighter than permitting every participant its own full cap. At B=0, T vanishes and the independent base extrema can be attained.

For integer t>=1 the marginal is w_j*min(1,max(0,c_j-(t-1))). This is nonnegative and nonincreasing even when the cap c_j is fractional. Any allocation of b_j units selects the first b_j entries of chain j. The largest unseen marginal must be a chain head because every later entry is no larger. Popping the greatest head therefore obtains a globally greatest remaining marginal and exposes the next entry of that chain. By induction the heap selects a prefix-closed set of q=min(B,positive-entry count) largest gains, attaining the upper bound on any feasible allocation. Zeros need not consume the at-most budget.

Scalar equality with the shared DP follows separately for minus and plus signs before the old width/pruning proof is reused. Equal marginal choices may yield several allocation witnesses but do not change the scalar bound. The algorithm still reports every maximizing bin transcript and every affordable primary-risk subset; a heap tie order for allocation is not a license to discard those output ties. The exact sharp endpoint, with its separate local binary enumeration/cache/DP, remains unchanged. [C19,C20]

supplement.heading: S11. sequential-objective analysis formal translation and exact witness arithmetic
paragraphs: The theorem begins with a common feasible world set, deterministic public observations, identical feasible subset family, prices and hard path budget. Always-available immediate true-value reveals, no failure/delay, no repeated purchase and no additional chronology are substantive assumptions. Restrict the sequential policy to one precommitted subset and an explicitly common order. Map S to its open-loop reveal tree and that tree back to S. If observation functions are closed-bin correspondences at thresholds, model each feasible label explicitly on both sides.

A terminal-width bridge g(S,omega)=W(S,x_S(omega)) is then imposed. It can be encoded as absolute regression loss against zero with predictor W, but that synthetic construction is not the original learned prediction target. If every transcript has positive p_t, max W-E W=sum p_t(max W-W_t). Every term is nonnegative, so equality holds precisely when every feasible transcript width is constant for that subset. To preserve values for every policy, require this for every allowed subset. Accidental equality of optimizers under weaker conditions is possible and does not prove policywise equivalence.

With alpha=0 and a common hard budget, preserve secondary lex(price,mask) separately from the complete primary-risk tie collection. Positive additive price can select only the cheapest member of a primary-risk tie. A sufficiently small alpha can preserve an isolated finite lex optimum relative to positive risk gaps but cannot retain unequal-price primary ties as additive minimizers. An adversarial distributional supremum equals max g, but substitutes a robust problem for a fixed learned-distribution objective.

Example1 worlds are (A=0,y=0,p=1/4), (A=0,y=1,p=1/2), (A=1,y=0,p=1/4), with feature price1, hard budget1, alpha1/8. The fixed Bayes predictor has initial tie prediction0 and expected stop error1/2. Buying A leaves expected error1/4, so priced expected value1/4+1/8=3/8. The worst world still errs, producing buy worst value9/8 versus stop1. Delta=y width remains1 at empty and at the ambiguous A0 transcript; both subset worst risks are1. Twelve direct world checks cover two public policies and two subsets.

Example2 worlds are (A=0,B=1,y=0,p=1/2), (1,0,0,1/4), (1,1,1,1/4), with two unit prices, hard budget2 and alpha1/16. Query A, STOP at0, query B at1 gives zero error and expected price1+1/2=3/2; priced expected loss is3/32. Static AB has zero error and price2, hence1/8. Adaptive and static worst price2, error0 and worst width0 tie. Nine public policies and four subsets give39 direct world checks. The two examples total11 policies,6 subsets,51 world checks and zero new empirical samples.

The saved unrestricted binary policy count obeys F(n,h)=1+n*F(n-1,h-1)^2 with F(n,0)=1 in the always-affordable fixture: F(1,1)=2 and F(2,2)=9. A fixed predictor is not an extra prediction action. The theorem concerns restricted open-loop policies; the harness also enumerates allowed adaptive STOP trees to expose the class difference. No trained surrogate, original AO* implementation or W41 solver is executed in these witnesses.

supplement.heading: S15. Full terminal proof, boundary semantics and exact scope
paragraphs: Assumption ledger: immutable unique IDs; one common nonempty Omega; identical static per-ID relation; the same fixed subset; all selected items acquired once; immediate always-successful reveals; no chronology restriction; common terminal STOP; order-invariant terminal Delta or predictor; additive fixed prices and common hard Q. Feasible-world equality itself uses only the common conjunction. Claims about executed acquisition and price additionally need the acquisition/STOP/cost assumptions. These logical dependencies should not be collapsed.

For any omega in F_pi(b), each i in M occurs at position pi inverse(i), so R_i(omega,b_pi_inverse(i)) holds. At sigma's position j, i=sigma_j and T(b)_j is exactly this same label. Thus every required sigma atom holds and omega belongs to F_sigma(T(b)). Interchanging pi and sigma proves reverse inclusion. Composition gives b_pi_inverse(sigma_sigma_inverse(pi_j))=b_j. The transformation therefore preserves both feasible and impossible tuples; no label mass is silently discarded.

For any equal nonempty feasible sets F, the sets {Delta(omega):omega in F} coincide. Their infima and suprema, and therefore widths, coincide. On the stored bounded closed polytopes with a finite binary component, the extrema are attained. The bijection transports every width maximizer in both directions; retaining one representative is insufficient when complete ties are requested. After fixing the same affordable subset family, equality of every R and C transports primary subset ties as well as the lex representative.

At a threshold t the original bins are [0,t] and [t,1]. A boundary value may therefore appear in both labels. Keep the relation, or introduce an expanded world carrying a fixed admissible label assignment, consistently on both sides. One cannot break a tie differently because a coordinate was asked first. The saved boundary point (1/5,1/2,4/5) has sum 3/2 and belongs to all four queried-label pairs for IDs0 and2; it confirms overlap was preserved rather than rounded away.

A=action trace and D=solver diagnostics remain outside this proof. Equal order and common reveal/STOP rules give the same A by a position-by-position induction, with coupled worlds/labels fixed. Equal A that retains all item IDs forces equal order by inspection of each position. Different order can share the same terminal ID reading without the same prefix worlds, bounds, cache state, first incumbent or work. None of those computational equalities follows from conjunction commutativity.

Empty M has one empty tuple, F=Omega, C=0 and one worst-tuple tie; an invalid empty Omega is rejected. These semantics do not supply the previously missing h=0 policy-generation complexity argument. Likewise a pushforward prior preserves expectation across two static orders only; equality of expectation and maximum additionally requires the W42 full-support/constant-width condition, which the W44 unequal widths fail to provide.

Pointwise k_i/4<=1[k_i>0]<=k_i gives C<=V<=min(1,4C). W maximizes after averaging each head and is not the average of a per-cycle maximum. Let F be fixed-policy mean, A mean all-mask oracle, P mean pair oracle and G actual gate mean. H=F-A>=0, E=P-A>=0, R=G-P>=0, so G-F=-(F-A)+(P-A)+(G-P)=-H+E+R. The historical actual fallback(3,100,0,90) was separately found in T. The conditional bound therefore covers this saved bank but not arbitrary compositional predictors. V24 directly compared the four-component prediction vectors for masks4 and5 over421 cycles, rather than inferring vector identity from matching error counts. They agree pointwise. For any common loss of(prediction,label,cycle), any normalized nonnegative cycle weights w_i, nonnegative source prices and lambda, and possibly randomized larger-mask probabilities q_i, risk difference is lambda*c_PS1/Z*sum_i w_i q_i>=0, Z=sum prices>0. This edition did not acquire full raw datasets for Hydraulic/HAR/Gas, perform their missingness/feature EDA, infer unknown physical axes or recover unobserved acquisition failures. supplement.heading: S27. Abstract
paragraphs: ProbeFlow studies when buying more information improves a frozen prediction system, and when the available evidence can support that conclusion. This cumulative edition connects the original shared-source acquisition design, exposed Hydraulic development studies, participant-separated HAR and MHEALTH controls, and the exact robust information-design program through research wave 42. These are different studies with different estimands; they are connected by their information, objective and accounting contracts, rather than pooled as one performance benchmark.

The controlled MHEALTH study evaluated 527 windows from two participants after a joint policy release. Conditional routing tied its strongest development-selected myopic baseline exactly, used only one second-group type, and failed its branch-support gate. Later waves quantified the resulting missing-fallback and availability uncertainty, constructed an exact pre-observation minimax subset selector, and proved safe strict pruning, shared-error-cap envelopes and an implicit marginal heap. Exactness preserved all primary ties; it did not establish application benefit. Reduced endpoint counts sometimes accompanied greater CPU, storage and output costs. Wave 42 separated sequential expected prediction loss from fixed-subset worst interval width with a conditional translation and two finite witnesses. Independent physical cost, new participant utility, original-method version identity, canonical ordered-trace correspondence and parts of the general complexity accounting remain unresolved. This edition performs documentary synthesis only.

This complete edition incorporates the W44 terminal-permutation result into those same contracts. A bijection between ID-indexed terminal readings preserves the feasible worlds, endpoints, additive price and complete worst ties under static, always-available reveals. It preserves neither literal action order nor solver prefix diagnostics. One stored W41 subset has worst width 3/5 and price 2 in both orders (no_gain); a separate two-item deadline construction completes 0/4 versus 4/4 schedules under the same changed conditions. Eight static encodings and eight deadline rows, plus rechecks, are not independent experiments. The W42 review statements below are dated evidence; the new terminal theorem narrows one semantic question without closing the original intake hold, general correspondence, complexity or application-evidence gaps. [C23-C28]

The W45-W47 return to a frozen mask-aware predictor is integrated without replacing the earlier identification and exact-solver results. W45's timed main failed after8 completed paths out of4152 planned; W46 completed1800 paths on120 exposed DEV windows but failed its two-action support gate. W47 completed8384 paths for16 policies on524 exposed windows from two people. Action-local support admission restored41 purchases relative to a same-run blanket guard, correcting16 errors with25 error ties and no guard-subset harms. The candidate nevertheless equals local myopic on every window, harms39 initially correct windows overall, and has higher declared objective than strong support-gated fixed subset/order controls. These are development diagnostics, not independent confirmation, a nonmyopic advance or a general safety result. New descriptive EDA inspects frozen feature arrays only; no study/model replay, fit or inference is performed. [C30-C35]

supplement.heading: S28. Acquisition motivation and the cumulative question
paragraphs: The original acquisition question is practical: a source may support several analyses, while its physical acquisition, internal computation and public disclosure occur at different times. Before adding a deeper planner, ProbeFlow asks whether the fixed predictor can use the permitted evidence, whether the chosen loss represents the intended decision, and whether a strong affordable baseline already produces the same result. The cumulative contribution is an auditable sequence of answers and failures to these questions, rather than an assertion that a more elaborate policy must be better.

The earliest archived v5 manuscript separates disclosed values z and mask m from acquired sources O, computed modules C, availability v, remaining budget b and required public failure history. A hidden cached prerequisite can reduce a later charge without authorizing its disclosure. Conversely, revealing one statistic need not reveal every statistic computed from the same raw trace. The state (z,m,O,C,v,b) is sufficient only under a history-consistent observation and transition model; it is not a universal Markov-state theorem. [C01]

This account therefore has three linked questions. First, do completed offline controlled observations demonstrate useful conditional acquisition? Second, what can be identified when required counterfactual outcomes are missing? Third, how can an exact solver choose a fixed information subset before its readings, without importing unavailable outcome information? The last question is a theory problem motivated by the earlier failures. Its solution does not retrospectively make those empirical failures successes.

The result is organized around one continuous chain: acquire only permitted information; preserve negative controls and unobserved counterfactuals; optimize a precisely declared uncertainty objective; and distinguish a terminal information set from a history of actions. The latest theorem addresses the last distinction. It is part of the same information contract, rather than an appended claim of empirical progress.

supplement.heading: S29. Objectives, information rights and comparable policies
paragraphs: An acquisition quote, a prediction error, an interval width and a physical resource bill are separate quantities. Shared-source accounting charges a raw acquisition once while keeping computation and disclosure rights explicit; the later minimax studies instead price guaranteed availability queries. Neither ledger measures sensor energy, clinical benefit, money or actual communication delay. A cheaper logical transcript is evidence about its declared accounting contract, and requires an additional physical measurement contract before it can support a deployment saving.

For an offline episode let pi use only the purchased public features and a frozen predictor f. A common secondary objective is J=mean(error)+lambda*mean(quotes), with the same lambda, price units, hard attempt cap and STOP privilege for every competing policy. Participant-macro objectives average each participant mean equally; pooled window objectives weight people by their number of retained windows. Their rankings need not agree. Training, calibration, selection, prediction inference, acquisition, audit and authoring costs also have different scopes. [C02,C07]

For the later robust problem, S is fixed before seeing query readings. Each feasible complete reading z induces a sharp interval [L(S,z),U(S,z)] for the route-minus-static macro loss difference Delta. Its risk is R(S)=max_z(U-L). Under query budget Q select lexicographically (R(S),sum prices,numeric mask), while separately returning every affordable subset tied in primary risk. A costlier primary tie remains part of the output even when the canonical answer is cheaper. There is no learned prior over these readings and no observation-dependent subset change. [C08]

A comparison supports an algorithmic advantage only when predictor rights, information, feasible policies, loss, aggregation, price and budget match. An exact same-information oracle must tie a correct exact selector. Pooling, an inaccessible outcome oracle, a different loss or an intentionally different policy class can diagnose a boundary, but cannot be relabeled an inferior implementation of the same task.

For order comparisons the public record is (S,z), where z maps immutable item IDs to labels. A positional tuple additionally depends on an order pi. The observation relation must stay the same when tuple positions change. Reindexing a tuple is permitted; replacing a chronological acquisition contract by a set of observations is a change of problem unless the static assumptions are established. [C23,C24]

supplement.heading: S30. Related work and the precise comparison boundary
paragraphs: Joint acquisition/classification with variable-size set encoding [shim2018] motivates representing the acquired information without granting unpurchased features to a policy. Generative-surrogate active feature acquisition [li2021,gsmrl-local-primary] supplies a sequential action/STOP/prediction formulation. ProbeFlow's current exact selector instead commits to a subset before readings and optimizes worst conditional uncertainty. These methods are related by an information-acquisition question, not by an established equivalence of losses, learned policies or implementations.

The cached GSMRL source expressly retains action chronology in time-series and real-world masking. A set-valued acquired-state notation alone does not remove schedule constraints. W44 read four saved intervals totaling 7,879 bytes concerning acquired sets, STOP, the terminal predictor and chronology. This is bounded local reading of an unversioned cache, not a fresh primary-paper reproduction. The missing declared W44 full-copy path and the actual preserved source hash are documented in the supplement. [C27]

Adaptive submodularity [adaptive-submodularity] gives guarantees under its own structural assumptions; the saved ProbeFlow complementarity witness violates diminishing returns for the present worst-width gain. Cawley and Talbot [cawley2010] motivate treating repeated model/policy selection as part of evaluation. Original AO* identity and guarantees remain an inherited unresolved primary-source comparison [inherited-author-index]. We claim no new external benchmark advantage, generic GSMRL/AO* equivalence or externally established novelty.

The separate bibliography verifier for this edition checked official metadata and selected current primary passages: Shim et al., NeurIPS31 (2018),1368-1378; Li and Oliva, PMLR139 (2021),6450-6459; Cawley and Talbot, JMLR11(70) (2010),2079-2107; and MHEALTH's UCI dataset citation (2014), DOI10.24432/C5TW22. A newly readable official GSMRL v2 page is a separate source from the old unversioned cache. The official AO* author index gives2002 while GSMRL v2 cites2004; original-body/pagination identity remains unresolved. The official adaptive-submodularity v5 comment reports a correction to Theorem13 with additional conditions; neither its revised proof nor a guarantee transfer is claimed. REFERENCES.json records exact reading and access limits.

supplement.heading: S31. Evidence lineage and units of inference
paragraphs: The historical evaluation lineage remains exposed. The Hydraulic studies repeatedly reused one rig and 421 evaluation cycles after earlier inspection; neither a chronological gap nor a newly frozen selection file creates an independent final sample. The later MHEALTH release recorded a local access boundary for two previously unparsed target participants, but its 527 windows and subsequent wave analyses still share those people and observations. More masks, predictions, scenarios or publication waves increase calculation records, rather than independent participants.

The preserved library begins with the v5 four-page source, followed by the v12 extended manuscript and v13 conference restructuring. V14 audited objective choice and a tuple-copy output ceiling; v15 broadened the output class; v16 jointly selected predictor and mask; v17 learned small gates; v18 and v19 retained the exposed-data setting while adding diagnostics. V19.1 changed reading diagrams, v20 separated main and supplement, v21 strengthened dominance checks, v21.1 repaired display encoding, and v22-v24 refreshed the argument. These publication version numbers are not autonomy wave numbers. [C01-C04]

The registered HAR, Gas and MHEALTH studies form the immediate empirical lineage of the autonomy campaign. The W1-W42 receipt inventory records accepted bounded results, an accepted failed result, operationally blocked starts and unattempted project slots separately. Carrying an earlier paper through another wave does not mean ProbeFlow executed in that wave. Accepted intake is a provenance/lifecycle fact, not scientific approval. The supplement and timeline preserve every wave status without replacing scientific history with operational incidents.

W44 adds two semantic witnesses, not two application datasets: the static witness reuses mask 5 of one previously stored seven-coordinate W41 environment, and the deadline witness uses two acquired IDs in four constructed bit worlds. The original eight static rows encode four distinct conjunctions twice; the eight deadline rows apply two schedules to the same four worlds. The author's sixteen raw-only checks and a separate coordinator arithmetic review reuse these observations. No row, recheck, saved policy or new document version adds an independent participant. [C25,C26]

supplement.heading: S32. What the Hydraulic lineage established and failed to establish
paragraphs: The three-channel Hydraulic replay first exposed a support failure: restoring marginal training labels did not restore useful selective coverage, and 391 of the 421 evaluation joint conditions were absent from the training prefix. In v12, removing a centroid prior offset reduced full-source component error from 0.723872 to 0.473872, with the entire 0.25 change confined to the cooler head. The selection-chosen nearest neighbor tied that full-source score. Under raw-sample prices TS1 matched full-source error at quote 60 rather than 6660; under equal source prices the selection-locked choice lost to a simple source/order control. These are exposed within-program observations. [C02]

The tuple-copy premise gave the v14 ceiling of 30/421 complete-vector successes. V15 permitted class-balanced per-head neighbor voting at k in {1,3,5,11,31}; it generated 25,000 prediction records and matched all 5,000 prior k=1 records. Selection still chose k=1, preserving all nine price-budget choices. An unselected k=3/mask3 diagnostic composed ten train-unseen tuples and reached 40/421 complete successes. This escapes the copying premise rather than refuting its conditional ceiling or validating the unselected model. [C03]

V16 joint predictor-mask selection changed three equal-price decisions but the strong TS1/k1 control still had one fewer component error. V17 fitted 390 gates on 102 policy-fit cycles, selected on another 102 cycles and evaluated 90 dependent settings on the same 421 exposed cycles. Its primary selector retained fixed PS1; a forced TS1-first gate matched TS1 component error while spending 22 extra quotes. Six k3-gate selections included four component improvements and two regressions, and all policy-fit targets shared one joint condition. V19-v24 then narrowed the conditional obstruction: the primary two leaves ultimately had identical four-head predictions on all 421 cycles, so any common prediction-label loss agrees and extra acquisition only adds nonnegative price. A secondary gate saved 63 component errors and 324 quotes while adding ten vector failures. No single aggregate turns that tradeoff into general utility. [C04]

supplement.heading: S33. Controlled HAR, Gas and MHEALTH observations
paragraphs: The HAR study fit on 14 participants and 4,996 windows, selected on seven participants and 2,356 windows, and evaluated the official nine-participant, 2,947-window test split. No candidate met the primary development error threshold 0.10, so the primary selected policy was null. A secondary cap-two gate reduced macro error by about 0.514 percentage points relative to strong fixed A while increasing mean quote from 1 to about 1.08127; its paths matched the same-STOP fixed order, three participants had worse error and four had worse secondary objective. The now-exposed test cannot become a new independent final for later edits. [C05]

The next Gas study opened batches 8-10 once under its joint release: 4,364 measurements, 3,277 errors and 4,364 quotes gave exact J=4369/5455. Routing and the strongest myopic policy both bought G4 and immediately stopped on every measurement. Their contrast was zero and the second-action denominator was zero. Naming a controller adaptive did not create adaptive behavior. [C06]

The same frozen predictor and the same development opportunities belong to the simple baselines as well as the proposed controller. MHEALTH routing, myopic acquisition and an ordered prefix executed identical target actions, and all 129 routing second decisions used the sparse-state unconditional fallback. The route-minus-strongest-baseline participant-macro contrast was exactly zero. Retaining the fixed G3+G4 policy with zero target errors at a higher logical quote exposes an objective tradeoff; it does not permit replacing the preselected primary comparator after release.

MHEALTH used subjects 1-3 for fifteen RF mask fits, subject 4 for temperature selection, 5-6 for action gains, 7-8 for policy selection and 9-10 for evaluation. The four positional groups were chest acceleration, ECG, ankle and wrist/lower arm, not four independent devices. The group definition avoided inferring the unresolved physical identity of duplicated/missing README axis entries. The 128-row nonoverlapping admission rule yielded 267 and 260 target windows. A sole frozen bank was shared with ChronoSense, making those projects dependent analyses of the same data. [C07]

The selected development policy had all 252 second decisions in G4; the target route likewise used G4 in all 129 second decisions, with 398 G3-to-STOP windows. The joint release explicitly permitted descriptive evaluation after the development support failure; it did not waive the adaptation-claim gate. Participant 9 supplied all 22 routing errors, all class 2 after STOP; participant 10 supplied none. Full-access RF had zero errors across 527 windows, while the full-access centroid had 34/267 and 22/260 errors. Those full-access diagnostics lie outside the cap-two policy contest and demonstrate neither conditional-routing gain nor clinical validity. The original outcome remains insufficient_support. [C07]

supplement.heading: S34. Missing counterfactuals led to partial identification
paragraphs: The stored MHEALTH traces contain no observed acquisition failure or late attempt. They also omit G3-only fallback predictions for the 129 windows on which the route requested G4, and do not identify the ranking of all eleven feasible subsets. W2 therefore computed eighteen conditional failure/penalty scenarios, preserving the strongest-myopic zero contrast. Its conditional break-even failure rate 9653/114400 at zero penalty relies on its loss-independence model; it is not an observed failure rate. [C09]

W5 removed that independence restriction. Across 36 coupling conditions it retained six universal static wins, nineteen nonidentified strict rankings and eleven universal route wins; its 72 endpoint witnesses were constructed, not observed failed acquisitions. W6 separated policy availability and shared versus separate fallbacks: 72 conditions split into 24 route wins, 24 static wins and 24 cases allowing both strict rankings. Equal average success is insufficient when window placement or fallback coupling differs. [C10]

W7 bounded unknown fallback errors rather than filling them with favorable predictions. Of 2,340 upper-count and 2,340 exact-count cells, 1,806 and 1,810 contracted; 534 and 530 did not. Exact counts created no additional strict-sign identifications in that grid. Even zero unknown errors left a zero-penalty half-success condition nonidentified. W8 then studied hypothetical availability intervals at known stop-error windows: 264 of 322 cells contracted, 58 did not, and all 92 placement negative controls had no gain. These are assumption-sensitive information results with zero new availability observations. [C11]

W10 preserved its first 41,860-cell raw calculation but was correctly marked failed: a temporary-path test unintentionally invoked the substantive main again, violating the single-main contract, and the second temporary raw was automatically removed. W11 did not erase that failure; a new bounded study calculated 29,120 cells, with 14,892 contractions and 14,228 ties against count-only information. W12 demonstrated that a parent simplified formula was nonsharp outside its slack regime in 4,913 of 6,548 constructed cells. The corrected joint optimization preserved infeasible scenarios and differences between exact counts and caps. [C12]

supplement.heading: S35. From identified intervals to a fixed minimax information design
paragraphs: W14 replaced a homogeneous-window shortcut with nonuniform window boxes, unequal participant sizes and a single shared cap B on unknown requested errors. It computed 3,636 cells; macro and pooled endpoints differed in 3,506, and copying the full cap to every participant was nonsharp in 912. Informative cells still included 974 no-gain outcomes, and 672 scenarios were infeasible. W15 made the query subset a decision variable fixed before readings, evaluating eight constructed designs, 368 subsets, 3,726 transcripts and 73 budget decisions. Information improved the specified worst width in 44 decisions and tied in 29; these are design choices, not new participants. [C13,C14]

In the current declared world model, participant j has n_j windows, requested set A_j, known stop-error set E_j and other stops O_j. Requested binary errors u share sum(u)<=B; u=1 on E and zero on O. Route availability r and static availability v are independent within-participant box/mean polytopes, each with sum n_j/2. For request indicator A, c=1/20 and k>=0, route loss is (1-A*r)u+c(1+A)+kA(1-r), static loss is (1-v)u+2c+k(1-v). Delta averages the per-participant differences. Querying coordinate i returns a guaranteed closed bin [0,t_i] or [t_i,1] for v_i. The bins overlap at t_i and the implementation preserves that semantics. [C08,C13]

The endpoint oracle minimizes and maximizes Delta over compatible original worlds. At fixed requested errors, each availability term is linear on a box intersected with one sum constraint: fill lower bounds, then allocate remaining mass in coefficient order. Enumerating local binary placements and convolving exact error counts across participants preserves one global cap. Independence of the declared participant/policy availability sets permits concatenating optimizers and hence sharp endpoints; it is a model assumption, not a discovery about real failures.

A change in a fixed program can explain a change in that program without identifying a physical mechanism or a population effect. The Hydraulic scoring-offset contrast, the MHEALTH RF-versus-centroid diagnostic and the finite availability models answer different controlled questions. None identifies the causal effect of purchasing a real sensor reading, corrects unknown physical metadata, or supplies the independent clinical or industrial utility evidence that the original acquisition motivation still requires.

supplement.heading: S36. Integrated procedure and module boundaries
paragraphs: The observation-dependent part must be stated precisely. An acquisition policy may react to revealed feature values, whereas the minimax query selector commits to its entire subset before any bin reading. Its internal enumeration of hidden losses supplies an adversarial bound, never information disclosed to the policy. Wave 42 deliberately compares these policy classes and shows that adaptive early stopping can change expected paid price even when final error, worst price and worst conditional width remain tied.

The integrated scientific procedure has an empirical observation layer and a robust-design layer. The empirical layer freezes predictor/development access and evaluates observable paths and failures. The robust layer consumes only a validated public model of the unresolved quantities; it does not read an unobserved fallback prediction as though it had been measured. The sharp endpoint routine, prefix traversal, optional envelope allocator and budget selector have distinct contracts. Saved raw records support a separately written original-loss arithmetic audit. [C08,C15-C18]

Operationally the preserved studies use source/contract seals, exact owned output directories, single-attempt stage records and explicit failed, unknown, impossible and unstarted states. A source mismatch, malformed public field, infeasible box, resource breach or ambiguous call is retained, rather than silently repaired or retried. Those local guards are cooperative code boundaries; timeout and path checks are not OS security isolation, external preregistration or scientific certification.

The terminal-permutation adapter is a representation boundary between an ordered tuple and an ID-keyed reading, not a new acquisition planner. It validates identical unique-ID subsets, reindexes every full label, preserves impossible/feasible status and all ties, and leaves the original action and solver diagnostic records untouched. In deadline or history-dependent settings it returns a failed static-assumption comparison instead of applying the quotient. [C23-C26]

algorithm.name: Integrated ProbeFlow procedure: freeze, observe, identify and design
inputs: Frozen predictor and explicit public acquisition/STOP/cost contract; training, development and evaluation access ledger.

outputs: Observable policy contrasts and their support/failure denominators; or stated insufficient_support/no_gain.
Under the declared world model: exact fixed-subset risks, all worst transcript ties, canonical affordable choice and all affordable primary-risk ties.
steps: Freeze predictor, observation rights, loss, aggregation, prices, candidate selection and source versions before the relevant evaluation release.
Run only authorized empirical acquisition stages; retain attempts, STOP paths, missing counterfactuals, participant errors and cost scope. A zero branch denominator cannot demonstrate routing gain.
Represent unresolved requested losses and availability as explicit compatible worlds; reject hidden outcome inputs and unverified guaranteed-bin claims.
For each precommitted query subset traverse feasible bin transcripts, using exact sharp endpoints at leaves and safe outward prefix envelopes only for the inner width maximum.
For the shared envelope use exact local-cap allocation by DP or the proved implicit marginal heap. Preserve the separate sharp endpoint routine and per-solver cold-cache rights.
Prune only if a prefix upper width is strictly below an already completed leaf incumbent. Expand equality and keep every worst transcript tie.

If comparing static orders, validate the common item-ID set and observation relation, then reindex terminal tuples by ID before comparing endpoints/full ties. Keep action order and solver diagnostics as separate outputs; do not apply this step across schedule-dependent feasibility.
Apply each hard query budget to the completed risk table; minimize (risk,price,mask) and separately return every affordable primary-risk tie.
Audit original-world arithmetic and full output partitions from saved records, retain failed/no_gain/cost-regression results, and state the scope still requiring independent application evidence.

supplement.heading: S37. Exactness, safe pruning and why greedy transfer fails
paragraphs: The worst-width information objective does not inherit a greedy approximation guarantee merely because its subject is information acquisition. The preserved complementarity witness has R(4)=R(5)=R(6)=3/8 and R(7)=1/4, so the same added item has marginal gain zero at one subset and 1/8 at a larger subset. A stale zero marginal is therefore not a certified future upper bound. Safe pruning instead follows containment of compatible worlds and preserves equality branches when all worst transcripts are required.

For prefix h and completion z, compatible worlds satisfy Omega_z subset Omega_h. Thus L(h)<=L(z)<=U(z)<=U(h), so prefix width is an upper bound for every descendant width. The largest completed feasible leaf width b is a lower bound on R(S). Cutting only U(h)-L(h)<b preserves the maximum and every maximizing complete label. Equality pruning can lose ties even when the numeric optimum is unchanged. This is an inner maximization certificate, not a lower bound that can discard a subset from the outer minimization. [C15,C16]

W18 verified the complementarity and heuristic boundary on three synthetic cases: 84 subsets and 819 readings, of which 730 were feasible and 89 impossible. A cost-ratio heuristic incurred regret 1/60 on a declared budget trap. W19 preserved 108 subset risks, five budget choices and all worst labels after strict pruning, but fewer feasible leaves (837 to 642) required more endpoint calls (837 to 1370) and more raw node bytes (183,934 to 287,257). A correct bound alone was not a compute saving. [C15,C16]

W21 derived a cheaper outward local envelope, exact at B=0. Endpoint calls fell from 785 to 741 across its four conditions, but two conditions had no endpoint gain and total nodes, CPU and retained output regressed. W22 then made the objective/backup distinction explicit: expected-cost AND/OR search, worst-transcript width search, upper/lower certificates and primary-tie contracts must agree before a solver correspondence is claimed. Its two conditions tied endpoint counts at 17 while prefix nodes rose from 18 to 28. [C17,C18]

supplement.heading: S38. Shared-cap dynamic programming and the implicit heap
paragraphs: For each participant the local outward envelope yields a base interval and one correction curve per sign f_j(b)=w_j min(b,c_j), where w_j=1/(P*n_j), 0<=b<=a_j, c_minus=a_j-l_A and c_plus=h_A. W39 combines these curves with sum b_j<=B by exact dynamic programming, tightening the cap-relaxed envelope. It still relaxes local coupling, so its interval is generally not the sharp endpoint interval. The established containment is L_relaxed<=L_shared<=L_sharp<=U_sharp<=U_shared<=U_relaxed. At B=0 the corrections vanish and the base is attainable under the declared independent model. [C19]

W41 observes nonnegative nonincreasing marginal chains delta_j(t)=w_j min(1,max(0,c_j-(t-1))). For each sign, initialize the first positive marginal from each chain in a heap, repeatedly pop the greatest and advance only that chain, stopping after B pops or no positive gain. The selected positive marginals form prefixes and attain the sum of the globally greatest available gains. Any feasible at-most-B allocation chooses chain prefixes and cannot exceed that sum. Therefore heap and DP scalar corrections agree exactly; allocation tie choices do not replace the required transcript/subset ties. This restates the saved theorem, rather than adding a new empirical result. [C20]

W39 used one heterogeneous two-participant, five-coordinate structure and two cap conditions: 64 risks, 486 complete labels and 20 budget decisions. At B=1 the shared bound reduced endpoint calls from cap-relaxed 208 to 201, with the same 480 linear calls and the same single-observation CPU, while strong sharp-prefix caching needed only 121 endpoints. W41 used one three-participant, seven-coordinate structure: 256 risks, 4,374 complete labels and 26 budget decisions across two cap conditions. The ten solver-condition records were complete, but B=2 all thirteen budgets tied the empty subset in risk. These quantities are constructed verification denominators. [C19,C20]
